{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-y4ad","title":"DeadDrop after/expires use monotonic default clock","description":"File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: correctness

DeadDropResource.__init__ defaults time_func to time.monotonic().
Drop created timestamps, age_s, GET ?after, and SenML expires all
use that same clock.

Spec 18.9 GET query is ?after=17216... (unix). LCI 17.5.8 POST
example uses SenML n=expires as unix 1721736400. _extract_ttl does
remaining = expires - now. drops() filters
drop["created"] <= after.

With the default monotonic now (uptime seconds, ~1e6-1e7):
- unix after=1721650000 compares against created~uptime, so
  created <= after is true for every drop and the filter drops
  the whole collection
- unix expires - monotonic now is ~1.7e9 seconds, clamped to
  DEADDROP_MAX_TTL (7d) instead of remaining wall time
- expires in the past does not expire; _extract_ttl falls through
  to DEADDROP_DEFAULT_TTL (24h)

Tests pass because they inject _Clock() at unix-epoch values,
hiding the default-clock mismatch.

Acceptance: default construction honors unix after/expires as
specified; keep monotonic (or equivalent) only for the 6/hour
rate window.
